newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria stakes out economy as diplomatic priority.
newsitem.headline: Algeria stakes out economy as diplomatic priority.

text.p: Algeria's president, whose country celebrated on Tuesday its National Diplomacy day for the first time, urged national diplomats to focus on Algeria's economic interests.

"Our diplomacy must concentrate more on the economic reach in its activities without neglecting its usual missions," said President Liamine Zeroual quoted by Algerian state-run radio as he adressed an official ceremony in Algiers.
Zeroual awarded nine veteran diplomats the highest national order of merit, including four posthumous awards.

One of these was awarded to the late foreign minister Seddik Benyahia, who was killed in a still mysterious plane crash in the 1980s near the border between Iraq and Iran while travelling to mediate in the first Gulf war.

State media marked the day by highlighting Algerian diplomatic breakthroughs in some prickly international disputes such the release of American diplomats from a 444-day siege in Teheran by revolutionnary Moslem fundamentalists in 1980.
Diplomacy Day coincided with the recognition of Algeria as a member of the United Nations 34 years ago, three months after independence from French colonial rule.

Algeria built its diplomacy since then by first forging close links with neighbouring countries in the Maghreb, then with the Arab world, with Moslem nations, Mediterranean Europe and then other areas.

It is current chairman of the Maghreb Arab Uunion (UMA) set up in 1989 with Morocco, Mauritania, Tunisia and Libya to bring closer their economies and diplomacies as a bargaining power in the face of the European Union across the Mediterranean.
Algeria is also the present chairman of the Arab League.
